newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end almost flat, Manila peso ignored.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end almost flat, Manila peso ignored.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed a fraction higher on Friday as gains of small-cap shares were mostly offset by losses of blue chips and other heavyweights, brokers said.
News on the Philippines' effective devaluation of the peso was generally ignored in the view that its impact on South Korean economy would be limited, brokers said.
Jinro Group firms gained on hopes that the group's plan to sell part of its affiliates and real estates would help ease financial troubles at the group.
The composite index closed 0.53 points higher at 768.30.
"It's a general view among investors that South Korean firms have only a limited exposure to peso-denominated securities," said Don Lee, an analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
Brokers said institutional investors continued to hesitate on uncertainty over the market's short-term course.
"Last week's brisk June trade figures strengthened optimism for the economic recovery, but investors are now waiting for follow-up signs," said Chung Chang-shik of Dongsuh Securities.
Ssangyong Oil Refining was unmoved by news that the oil refinery had signed an agreement to export 1.8 million barrels of gasoline to Saudi Arabia's state-run Saudi Aramco.
Ssangyong shares closed down 400 won at 18,500.
Jinro Ltd was up 340 won to 7,520, Jinro Industries Co up 200 won to 5,270 and Jinro General Foods up 30 won to 4,400.
The Jinro Group said on Thursday it would sell 12 of its 18 affiliates and some of its real estate this year to generate more than 840 billion won.
September index futures closed down 0.20 of a point at 80.80 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index shed 0.09 to 79.55.
